samples.summary: Nothing tests that reading a client-key salt refreshes its timestamp, so a regression silently rotates the key after 30 days of daily use and orphans unsent offline work
samples.evidence: `deviceSecret()` rewrites `{s, t: now}` when `now - stored.t >= SECRET_TOUCH_MS`, and the module comment states this is what "keeps the sweep honest in both directions: a document this device actually opens never expires out from under its own stored entry". Every salt-lifetime case in `durable-session.test.ts` instead writes a stale entry directly (`localStorage.setItem("wafflebase-durable-device:u1:note-7", JSON.stringify({ s: ..., t: stale }))`, lines ~156-200) and asserts the expiry/sweep. The only case that reads a salt twice is "keeps the same key across reloads of this device", which calls `durableClientKey` twice within the same millisecond — the touch branch is never entered and never asserted. If the touch were dropped or inverted, a document opened daily would still have its salt aged out 30 days after *mint*: `durableClientKey` returns a new salt, the SDK's store scope `apiKey/clientKey/docKey` changes, and the entry holding un-pushed changes becomes unreachable and is later collected — the offline work loss this feature exists to prevent. `deviceSecret` uses `Date.now()` directly with no injectable clock (unlike `WafflebaseDocStore`, which takes `now`), which is likely why no test drives it; `vi.useFakeTimers()` would work here since nothing in this path is IndexedDB-backed.

samples.summary: Four of the five lapse reasons the durable client can publish (`too-large`, `out-of-space`, `write-failed`, `unreportable`) are asserted nowhere, though the design requires the tooltip to name the case
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` computes `lapse` from `lost → 'dropped'`, `persistDisabled → 'too-large'`, `outOfSpace → 'out-of-space'`, `writesFailing → 'write-failed'`, `unreportable → 'unreportable'`. `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` drives every one of those state transitions (`onWriteFailure`, `persist-disabled`, refused subscriptions) but its only consumer is `function Probe() { return {useDocumentDurability() ? 'durable' : 'not-durable'} }` — it never reads `useDurabilityLapse`, so only the boolean is checked. `sync-status-chip.test.tsx` asserts the sentences but injects each lapse by hand via `DurabilityLapseScope`, and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`'s "lets the durable client overrule the call site, from the real providers" covers only `'dropped'`. The `out-of-space` arm is the most exposed: `onWriteFailure` sets both `outOfSpace` and `writesFailing`, so only the ordering of the ternary distinguishes "This device is out of local storage space" from "This device could not be written to", and nothing asserts that ordering. Cost if wrong is a wrong (but non-destructive) diagnosis in the tooltip the design explicitly requires to name the case.

samples.summary: `hasOfflinePersistenceConsent()` is new and has no direct test; its false branch — the one that lets an editor render immediately on a device nobody has opted in on — is uncovered
samples.evidence: `offline-persistence-preference.test.ts` covers `get`/`set`/`subscribe`/the memory mirror, but grep for `hasOfflinePersistenceConsent` across `packages/frontend` returns only the definition and its single call site (`collab-document-provider.tsx:241`). It is exercised indirectly in exactly one true-branch case — `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`'s "waits for the identity rather than reading a pending one as 'not eligible'", which sets `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled('7', true)` before making the identity pending. The complementary case the source comment promises — "A device where nobody has is still decided instantly" (identity pending, no consent ⇒ `mayPersist` false ⇒ `identified` true ⇒ render now) — has no test: "renders immediately when the feature is off" runs with `me.isPending = false`, so it passes whatever `hasOfflinePersistenceConsent` returns. If that function regressed to always-true, every editor would render `null` until the `['me','optional']` query settles — a blank frame in front of every document once the client-key pin is bumped.

samples.summary: The `saved-locally` info toast is tested only for emission; its latch and the recovery arm that retracts it once the work reaches the server are untested
samples.evidence: The new effect branch sets `warned.current = true` and emits `toast.info(..., { id: TOAST_ID })`, and the comment says it is latched "so the recovery arm below retracts this one too and confirms once the work actually reaches the server". `sync-status-chip.test.tsx`'s `describe('SyncStatusChip on a durable document')` asserts the info toast is raised ("says where the work went instead of saying nothing") but no case drives the document back to `saved` afterwards to assert `toast.dismiss(TOAST_ID)` + the `RECOVERY_TOAST_ID` success — grep for `RECOVERY_TOAST_ID` in that file returns nothing. The equivalent behaviour is covered for the `not-saved` path only. Shared code path, so the blast radius is a stale 'Saved to this device' toast rather than data loss.

samples.summary: The `navigateRef` indirection — the reason the housekeeping effect does not re-run on every in-app navigation — has no test
samples.evidence: The component deliberately holds `navigate` in a ref and keeps it out of the effect deps, with a comment naming the cost of getting it wrong: "a new database handle, the thirty-day sweep again, the archive listing again, and a title fetch per archive — for an identity that has not changed. The toast id dedupes what the user sees, which is exactly why the repetition would go unnoticed." `offline-runtime.test.tsx` never re-renders the component with a changed `navigate` identity (every case does a single `render(<OfflineRuntime userId="42" />)`), and the `react-router-dom` mock returns one stable `navigate` fn, so the effect could take `navigate` as a dependency and every case would still pass. A regression is silent by construction — repeated unfiltered `GET /documents` and repeated sweeps per navigation, invisible to the user.

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser` — the only thing scoping the orphan-snapshot sweep across accounts — is exercised by no test with a key that matches its pattern
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters with `!this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)`, which parses `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` out of the store key. The only orphan test is `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts` "is collected rather than living forever out of reach", which seeds `doc-a` — a key the regex cannot match, so the predicate returns `false` on the fall-through path and the test passes whether the parse is right, wrong, or removed. No case seeds an orphan under a realistic `pk/wb:{secret}:{otherUser}:sheet-7/sheet-7` key to assert this user's sweep spares it, and none seeds one under this user's own `wb:` key to assert it is still collected (the safe-direction claim in the comment). If the regex drifted so it matched this user's own keys, the orphan repair would stop running entirely and `load` would keep reporting a permanently unwritable document as present.

samples.summary: The Settings switch's no-identity behaviour (`disabled={!userId}` and the `if (!userId) return` guard) has no test
samples.evidence: `tests/app/settings-offline.test.tsx`'s `render()` helper unconditionally seeds `client.setQueryData(['me'], { id: 7, ... })`, so every case runs with a resolved identity and `userId` is never `undefined`. The comment on the prop states the harm it prevents — "a choice made with nobody signed in would be written nowhere while the switch showed it as on" — but nothing asserts the switch is disabled, or that clicking it writes nothing, while `['me']` is unresolved or the query failed. The guard could be deleted and the suite stays green.

samples.summary: `keepArchives` and `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` are options no caller passes and no test exercises
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` forwards to `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1135`, branch at :1173), and the doc comment there describes the caller as "a session the server expired" — but this diff changes the 401 arm to erase nothing at all (`eraseLocalData: "none"`), so that caller no longer exists. Grep for `keepArchives` across `packages/frontend` returns only the two signatures, the branch and the comments: no call site, no test. Same for `dropArchivesWhere(index, range, onlyUser)` at `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1363` — both call sites omit `onlyUser`, so the intersection logic it guards is never executed. Unreachable today, so the impact is confined to the option being wrong when someone does wire it up.

samples.summary: "offers it back once access has been reconciled" asserts nothing its neighbours do not already assert, and nothing about the ordering its name claims
samples.evidence: The case body is `listRecoverableWork.mockResolvedValue([...]); render(...); await waitFor(() => expect(toastWarning).toHaveBeenCalled()); expect(purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments).toHaveBeenCalled();`. Both facts are already established by "offers work that could not be saved, without creating anything" and "drops copies of documents the server no longer lists". Nothing here observes *order* — no `mock.invocationCallOrder` comparison, no sequencing assertion — so the case would pass even if the recovery offer ran before the reconcile. The property it names is actually covered by its two siblings ("offers nothing back when the reconcile could not run" / "...when the purge itself failed"), which is why this is a nit rather than a coverage gap.

samples.summary: The traversal suite's id-encoding assertion is weakened from every request to at least one request
samples.evidence: The loop `for (const raw of urls) { ...; expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)); }` became `expect(paths.some(p => p.includes(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)))).toBe(true)`. The weakening is defensible — `deleteWorkspace` now issues a companion `fetchDocuments()` carrying no id — and the load-bearing half (`expect(pathname).not.toContain("/auth/logout")` over every path) is still asserted for all requests, so a dropped `seg()` on any id-bearing request is still caught via `..` normalization. Recorded only because the suite is the repo's traversal guard and the assertion it relies on is now positional rather than universal; an id-bearing request that stopped being made at all would no longer be noticed as long as one other request still carries it.

samples.summary: The module-scope `storage` listener's `event.key === null` arm (whole storage area cleared) is untested
samples.evidence: The listener clears `memoryConsent` when `event.key === null || event.key === STORAGE_KEY`, with the comment "A `null` key is the whole area being cleared, which includes ours". `offline-persistence-preference.test.ts` drives a `StorageEvent` for `STORAGE_KEY` ("yields to another tab after a write of ours failed") and for an unrelated key ("keeps the mirror when another key changes"), but never for `key: null`. Consequence if dropped is a stale session mirror after a site-data clear in another tab — cosmetic and self-correcting on reload.

verdict.reason: The touch-on-read branch in deviceSecret (durable-session.ts:276-278) rewrites the stored timestamp when an entry is older than SECRET_TOUCH_MS, and the module comment (lines 265-268) presents this as the guarantee that a document opened regularly never ages out of its own salt entry. No test exercises it. In durable-session.test.ts the salt cases (lines 84-213) either plant an entry already 31 days stale and assert expiry/sweep (155-162, 168-181), assert forgetDeviceSecret (124-134, 183-205), or call durableClientKey twice in the same tick ("keeps the same key across reloads", 207-213) which never enters the touch branch and never inspects the stored timestamp. offline-erase.test.ts:96-129 and 316-340 read the same localStorage entries only for presence/absence after an erase. A repo-wide grep for the storage prefix returns only those two test files, the source, and a design doc; a grep for the 1-day constant returns no test-side use; and every other module importing durableClientKey (use-durable-document, durable-yorkie-provider, collab-document-provider-identity/-durable, offline-runtime tests) neither plants salt entries nor drives a clock for this path. Deleting or inverting lines 276-278 would leave every suite green while a daily-used document's salt aged out 30 days after mint, changing the SDK store scope apiKey/clientKey/docKey and orphaning un-pushed offline changes — a data-affecting gap, so major, and squarely in the missing-tests lane.
